source.summary: The two portraits are either too separated or too weak; preserve the approved typography and orbital line.

changes.instruction: Reduce displacement and raise visibility until it is discoverable only after the primary face reads.
changes.reason: The current four-eye read destroys the intended delayed narrative discovery.

preserve.invariant: Keep geometry, spacing, position, and tonal relationship unchanged.
Keep identity, crop, expression, and first-read dominance unchanged.

prohibit.outcome: Four equally strong eyes appear at thumbnail scale.
prohibit.consequence: The image reads as a malformed face instead of delayed double exposure.

prohibit.outcome: The second portrait remains undiscoverable at normal use scale.

relationships.subject: primary portrait
relationships.intended_effect: The viewer first sees one person and then discovers two overlapping identities.
relationships.pass_condition: At 160 px the image reads as one face; at normal display size the second face becomes discoverable without producing two separate heads.

verification.method: Compare 160 px thumbnail and normal-size artifact with the parent checkpoint.
verification.pass_condition: The primary face controls first read and the secondary face controls second read.

verification.method: Overlay comparison against the approved parent.
verification.pass_condition: No unapproved geometry or identity drift is visible.
